newsitem.title: UK: UN invites Morocco, Polisario to direct talks.
newsitem.headline: UN invites Morocco, Polisario to direct talks.

text.p: U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan on Thursday invited Morocco and the Polisario Movement struggling for independence in Western Sahara to hold face-to-face talks in Lisbon on June 23.

Former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker, Annan's personal envoy, said after two days of talks with all those involved in the region that he believed the proposed Lisbon talks might be the last real chance of finding a solution to the area's problems.
"I have come to the conclusion that in the absence of direct talks between the parties involved, I do not think it (the UN settlement plan) can be concluded," Baker told reporters.
"Annan has invited Morocco and the Polisario for private talks in Lisbon on June 23," he said, adding that Algeria and Mauritania were being invited as interested party observers.
The United Nations has been trying for years to organise a referendum, originally set for January 1992, to decide whether Western Sahara should be incorporated into Morocco or become independent.
But the referendum, called for under a U.N. peace plan, has been repeatedly postponed because of a disagreement between the two sides over who should be eligible to vote.
